title: Is Amazon Prime Worth It for Buying a Dehumidifier?
h1: Is Amazon Prime Worth It When You're Buying a Dehumidifier?
dek: When a basement is wet, every day counts. Here's when Prime's fast, free delivery pays for itself — and when the free trial is all you need.
description: Is Amazon Prime worth it for dehumidifier shoppers? How fast shipping, free returns and the 30-day trial stack up when you need a heavy appliance quickly.
intro: Is **Amazon Prime worth it** if all you need right now is a dehumidifier? For many shoppers, yes — and the reason is speed more than streaming. Prime costs **$139 a year or $14.99 a month**, comes with a **30-day free trial**, and delivers eligible items in a day or two at no extra charge, even bulky 50-pint units. On a heavy appliance that might otherwise carry a freight charge, that can cover a good chunk of the fee on one order.

Buying a dehumidifier is unusually time-sensitive. A leaking basement or a musty crawl space isn't a someday project: the EPA notes that mold can start growing on a damp surface within **24 to 48 hours**. Waiting two weeks for a unit to arrive can mean the difference between drying out a room and tearing out drywall. Here's how to decide whether to join, use the trial or skip Prime entirely.

blocks.text: Industry estimates put US Prime membership well above 150 million people, so there's a fair chance someone in your household already has it. If so, check whether you can use their membership through an Amazon Household before paying for your own.

blocks.text: Here's the practical play. Once you've settled on a model from our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) picks, compare the delivery date and shipping cost with and without Prime. If you need it fast and it's a big, heavy unit, the math usually favors at least starting the trial.

items: **You rarely shop on Amazon.** If you buy an appliance every few years and little else, use the free trial for this purchase and let it lapse.
**The unit already ships free.** Many dehumidifiers include free standard shipping without Prime. If your space is only mildly damp, waiting a few extra days costs nothing.
**You don't want the extras.** Prime bundles video, music and reading perks. If you'd never use them, you're paying purely for shipping — run the numbers before committing to a full year.

**You need only a small unit.** For a single bedroom or closet, a compact dehumidifier is light and inexpensive enough that a full membership rarely pays off. See our [best small dehumidifiers](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: What to check on an Amazon dehumidifier listing

items.label: Who sells and ships it
items.text: Prime delivery and Amazon's standard return terms apply most cleanly to items sold or fulfilled by Amazon. Third-party sellers can set their own return policies.

items.label: The DOE 2019 capacity
items.text: Some listings quote inflated pint figures measured in hot, saturated air. Look for the DOE rating and size with our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.label: A real brand and model number
items.text: A full model number lets you check ENERGY STAR listings, manuals and CPSC recalls before you buy.

items.label: Drainage options
items.text: If there's no floor drain near the unit, filter for a built-in pump. Our [pump picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) are a good shortlist.

items.label: The return window
items.text: Confirm it before you order, especially for large or heavy units.

sections.heading: How to use the free trial the smart way

items: **Start the 30-day trial before you check out**, so the faster shipping applies to your order.
**Order everything at once** — the dehumidifier plus any drain hose, spare filter or hygrometer — so it all arrives together.
**Turn off auto-renew** in your account's Prime membership settings right away if you're not sure you want to stay.
**Decide before day 30** whether deals, returns and the other perks are worth the annual fee to you.

blocks.title: Other ways to pay less
blocks.text: Amazon offers discounted Prime Student memberships and a reduced-price Prime Access plan for people on qualifying government assistance. If either applies to you, check eligibility before paying the standard rate.

Speed only helps if you get the unit working quickly and correctly. Let a compressor model stand upright for a few hours if it was shipped on its side, then set it up in the right spot — our [placement guide](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) covers clearances and basement drainage. Set the humidistat to about 45–50% to start, and keep an eye on it for the first few days. If you're drying out a basement, our [basement picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) explain how to keep it dry for good.

For most people buying a dehumidifier, Prime is worth it at least for a month. Fast, free delivery on a heavy appliance gets the damp out sooner, and the 30-day trial lets you take advantage without committing to a full year. Keep the membership only if the year-round perks fit your life — and either way, don't let the mold clock run down while you wait for a delivery.

faqs.q: How much does Amazon Prime cost?
faqs.a: Prime is $139 a year or $14.99 a month in the US, and new members typically get a 30-day free trial. Discounted plans are available for students and for people on qualifying government assistance.

faqs.q: Is Amazon Prime worth it just to buy a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: If you need the unit quickly — say, after a storm leaves the basement wet — the free trial is almost always worth starting. Whether a full paid year makes sense depends on how much else you buy on Amazon.

faqs.q: Does Prime include free shipping on large dehumidifiers?
faqs.a: Generally, yes, on eligible listings that show the Prime badge, including heavier 50-pint units. Check the listing for the Prime label and the estimated delivery date.

faqs.q: Can I return a dehumidifier I bought with Prime?
faqs.a: Most dehumidifiers sold and fulfilled by Amazon can be returned within the standard return window. Third-party sellers set their own terms, so check the listing before you buy.

faqs.q: Can I cancel Prime after buying my dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Yes. You can cancel at any time, and if you cancel during the free trial you won't be charged. Turning off auto-renew right after signing up is the easiest way to avoid a surprise bill.
